17   EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

18          Q. What is the purpose of your rebuttal testimony?

19          A.   The purpose of my rebuttal testimony is to respond to the Office of the

20   Public Counsel’s (“OPC”) witness Dr. Geoff Marke’s direct testimony in regard to his

21   recommendation for the Critical Medical Needs Program (“CMNP”).




                                              Page 1
      Rebuttal Testimony of
     Amy L. Eichholz

1    CRITICAL MEDICAL NEEDS PROGRAM

2           Q.       What is the CMNP?

3           A.       The CMNP is designed to promote and finance a community-based

4    information resource network and program staff that will identify and direct customers

5    with critical medical needs to resources that will:

6                •   Help customers with maintaining or restoring utility services,

7                •   Avoid negative impacts on residents with serious medical conditions,

8                •   Address utility arrears, and

9                •   Provide a streamlined process to complementary services.

10   Additionally, the program provides outreach and training to community stakeholders that

11   will allow them to identify individuals that are critical medical needs for assistance and

12   refer such individuals to available assistance resources.

13          Q.       What is Evergy Missouri Metro, Inc., d/b/a Evergy Missouri Metro’s (EMM”)

14   proposal on the CMNP?

15          A.       Evergy Missouri Metro stated in response to Data Request 302 that they

16   have not proposed any changes to any of the current Low-Income Programs or its

17   customer eligibility requirements and has recommended to continue the programs

18   currently in effect as part of this case.

19          Q.       What is the current budget for the CMNP for Evergy Missouri Metro?

20          A.       The current budget is $300,000 with a 50/50 sharing between shareholders

21   and ratepayers.

22          Q.       What is OPC’s proposal on the CRMP?


                                                 Page 2
      Rebuttal Testimony of
     Amy L. Eichholz

1           A.     Dr. Marke proposes to increase funding level to $2 million (with a 50/50

2    sharing) for the CMNP and he recommends the tariff should be drafted to allow funding

3    to be fungible with other programs if spending stalls.

4           Q.     What is Staff’s response to Dr. Marke’s recommendation?

5           A.     EMM provided information on their Low-Income Programs in the

6    Low-Income Workshop Case No. OW-2026-0085. This information explained that the

7    EMM only spent roughly $71,000 of its total $300,000 CRMP budget in 2024. Therefore, it

8    is Staff’s opinion there is no need to increase the funding level to $2 million. Additionally,

9    Staff with would like to see the outcome of the Low-Income Workshop before proceeding

10   with any major changes to the current Low-Income programs, including allowing funding

11   to be moved to other programs.

12          Q.     Does this conclude your rebuttal testimony?

13          A.     Yes.




                                                Page 3
                                                        Amy L. Eichholz

                                   Education and Employment Background


         I am Research/Data Analyst of the Energy Resources Department, Industry Analysis

Division of the Missouri Public Service Commission. Prior to my current position, I was

employed at the Missouri Department of Natural Resources as an Environmental Program

Analyst from January 2022 through December 2022.

         I received a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Administration in December

1997, and a minor in Marketing, all from Lincoln University, Jefferson City, Missouri.


         Prior to first joining the Commission, I worked in various positions within three state

agencies of the State of Missouri. I was employed as an Executive II for the HIV, STD, and

Hepatitis Section of the Missouri Department of Health and Senior Services; as a Deputy

Clerk for the Supreme Court of Missouri; as a Game Accounting Executive, Administrative

Office Assistant, Inside Sales Representative, and a Licensing Specialist for the Missouri

Lottery. From September 1999 through December 2017.
